MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Employment Type: Permanent Full Time
Position Classification: Nurse Manager Grade 5 
Remuneration: $170,655.23 - $173,551.14 + Superannuation + Salary packaging 
Hours Per Week: 38
Requisition ID: REQ673097
Located in: Maitland Hospital 
Applications Close: Sunday the 19th of July 2026
*Tentative Interviews the week of the 20th

Be at the forefront of innovation in healthcare-leading medical services that are setting new standards for quality, safety, and impact.

Are you an accomplished nursing leader ready to influence healthcare at a strategic level?
This is an outstanding opportunity to step into a senior nursing leadership role where you'll have genuine influence over the future of healthcare delivery.
As Deputy Director of Nursing - Operational Nurse Manager Medical Services, you'll partner with executive leaders to oversee a complex portfolio encompassing Medical Services, Cancer Services and specialist nursing teams. You'll champion clinical excellence, inspire high-performing teams and drive innovation across one of New South Wales's newest and fastest-growing hospitals.

About the Role

This senior leadership position provides operational and professional leadership across a broad portfolio including:

Medical inpatient services

Cancer Services

Palliative Care Services

Clinical Nurse Consultants (CNCs)

Nurse Practitioners

McGrath Breast Care Nurses

A large and diverse team of specialist nursing services

You'll provide strategic oversight of workforce operations, clinical governance, financial performance and service delivery while ensuring safe, high-quality patient care across Medical Services. Working alongside executive, medical and multidisciplinary teams, you'll influence hospital-wide initiatives and contribute to the strategic direction of nursing services. Partnering with the executive leadership team, this role also participates in the hospital's on-call roster.

What You'll Be Doing

As Deputy Director of Nursing, you will:

Provide professional nursing leadership across Medical Services

Lead workforce planning, staffing profile management and operational performance

Drive clinical governance, patient safety and quality improvement initiatives

Manage budgets, resources and service performance against key organisational targets

Support and develop Nurse Unit Managers and specialist nursing leaders

Lead organisational change and service improvement projects

Partner with executive, medical and multidisciplinary stakeholders to deliver exceptional patient outcomes

Foster a culture of innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement.

About You

You are an experienced and strategic nursing leader who can inspire others while balancing operational priorities with long-term service planning.

You'll bring:

Current registration as a Registered Nurse with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia and appropriate tertiary qualifications, or working towards, and-or demonstrated relevant leadership or management experience.

Extensive leadership experience within a complex healthcare environment

Experience managing medical services, cancer services or a similarly complex clinical portfolio

Strong clinical governance and quality improvement expertise

Demonstrated experience managing workforce operations, budgets and resource allocation

Exceptional stakeholder engagement and communication skills

The ability to influence change, lead innovation and develop high-performing teams

A collaborative leadership style with a passion for mentoring future nursing leaders

Postgraduate qualifications in a relevant specialty are highly regarded.

Why Join Maitland Hospital?

Maitland Hospital is one of New South Wales's newest and fastest-growing health facilities, purpose-built to deliver contemporary, world-class care within a modern, state-of-the-art environment. Featuring advanced clinical spaces, leading-edge technology and ongoing investment in service expansion, it offers an outstanding setting for both patients and staff alike.

This is an opportunity to:

Join an executive leadership team shaping the future of one of NSW's newest hospitals

Lead a diverse portfolio encompassing Medical and Cancer Services

Drive strategic nursing practice and clinical governance across a growing health service

Influence hospital-wide decision making and organisational change

Work alongside passionate and collaborative clinical leaders

Access outstanding professional development and executive leadership opportunities within Hunter New England Health

"Our people are at the heart of everything we do. We know that exceptional patient care begins with a supported, skilled, and valued workforce. As Director of Nursing and Midwifery, I'm committed to fostering a workplace where collaboration, respect, and continuous learning are part of everyday practice. Whether you're starting your career or bringing years of experience, you'll be part of a team that cares for one another, grows together, and is proud of their workplace and proud to serve our community." - Luke Feenan - Director of Nursing and Midwifery
 

Additional Information

To be eligible for permanent employment in this position you must be an Australian Citizen, or a permanent resident of Australia, or a New Zealand citizen with a current New Zealand Passport. Employment of a temporary visa holder may only occur if no suitable local candidate is identified for the position; in this instance, you may only be offered employment in line with the conditions and expiry date of your visa.

We are unable to accommodate visa sponsorship for applicants requiring a visa for this position.

result.description:
Location: Palmerston, Northern Territory
Employment type: Full-time
Hours: 38 hours per week
Salary: $67,510 to $70,000 plus superannuation

About us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the business
The business (ABN 91 213 951 452) is a takeaway food outlet located in a busy shopping centre food court in Palmerston. They serve a range of freshly prepared takeaway products, including loaded chips, fish and chips, fried chicken, seafood baskets, hotdogs, ice cream and milkshakes.

They are seeking a reliable and hardworking Kitchenhand to support their food preparation and service team.

About the Role
The Kitchenhand will assist with basic food preparation, maintain clean and hygienic kitchen and service areas, wash utensils and equipment, receive supplies and support the preparation and service of takeaway food.

The position involves standing for extended periods, working in a fast-paced environment and safely handling kitchen equipment, cleaning products and food supplies.

The successful applicant must be available across a rotating roster, including weekends, public holidays and evening shifts where required.

Key Responsibilities
- Clean kitchen, food-preparation, storage and service areas. 
- Wash and sanitise cooking equipment, utensils, containers and other kitchen items.
- Assist with preparing ingredients for cooking and service.
- Portion, assemble and pack food items for customer orders.
- Assist with preparing simple menu items under direction.
- Cook, toast or heat simple food items in accordance with workplace procedures.
- Prepare takeaway packaging, food trays and service materials.
- Receive, transfer, weigh, check and correctly store food supplies.
- Rotate stock and assist with monitoring expiry dates and stock levels.
- Dispose of waste, clean bins and maintain waste-storage areas.
- Maintain clean floors, benches, sinks, fryers and other work areas.
- Assist kitchen and counter staff during busy service periods.
- Follow food-safety, allergen, hygiene and workplace health and safety procedures.
- Report equipment faults, stock shortages and safety issues to the supervisor.
- Complete opening, closing and cleaning duties as allocated.

Skills and Experience
The successful applicant must have:
- Previous experience as a Kitchenhand, food-preparation assistant or in a similar takeaway, hospitality or food-service role;
- Knowledge of basic kitchen hygiene and food-safety practices;
- The ability to follow instructions and workplace procedures;
- The ability to safely use cleaning products and basic kitchen equipment;
- Good attention to cleanliness and food-handling requirements;
- The physical capacity to stand for extended periods and perform repetitive manual duties;
The ability to work efficiently during busy service periods;
Good teamwork and communication skills;
A reliable and punctual approach to work; and
Availability to work weekends, public holidays and shifts according to the business roster.
A food-handling or food-safety certificate is desirable. Relevant workplace training may be provided.
How to Apply
To apply, submit the following:

Resume outlining your work experience and references.
A short cover letter (max. 300 words) explaining:
Why you are applying for this position; and
An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork (use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result).
A Written Response (max. 600 words) describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role you are applying for. Please structure your example(s) using the STAR method.
* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a busy and growing takeaway food business serving the Palmerston community, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Walk-in or telephone enquiries regarding this vacancy will not be accepted.

Applications close: 20 August 2026

Position Summary

We are seeking an experienced, high-energy, and hands-on Restaurant Manager to oversee the daily operations, financial performance, and guest experiences across our venue. As a key leader in our business, you will manage front-of-house staff, coordinate with the kitchen team, optimize profitability, and ensure strict compliance with health, safety, and licensing regulations.

Key Responsibilities and Duties

Operations Management: Direct and oversee the day-to-day operations of the venue to ensure exceptional customer service, smooth service flow, and high standards of hospitality.

Financial & Performance Control: Monitor and manage venue budgets, labour costs, and cost of goods sold (COGS). Analyze sales data, manage stock control, and implement strategies to maximize profitability.

Staff Leadership & Training: Recruit, train, schedule, and supervise front-of-house staff and supervisors. Foster a positive team environment, conduct performance reviews, and ensure staff adhere to service standards.

Compliance & Safety: Maintain strict compliance with workplace health and safety (WHS) regulations, food safety programs, and responsible service of alcohol (RSA) legislation.

Customer & Community Relations: Proactively manage customer feedback, resolve complaints efficiently, and build strong relationships with regular patrons to enhance the brand's local reputation.

Supplier Coordination: Liaise with suppliers, manage inventory ordering, and coordinate with the kitchen team to maintain stock levels and ensure seamless service.

Skills, Qualifications, and Experience Required

Education: An Associate Degree, Advanced Diploma, or Diploma in Hospitality Management (ANZSCO Skill Level 2); OR at least 3 years of relevant professional experience.

Experience: A minimum of 2–3 years of proven experience in a similar fast-paced restaurant management or supervisory role.

Technical & System Skills: Proficiency in modern point-of-sale (POS) management systems (e.g., Square for Restaurants or Lightspeed), staff scheduling platforms, and basic digital communication tools.

Compliance Certification: Valid Western Australia Approved Manager Licence (or ability to obtain one), Responsible Service of Alcohol (RSA) certificate, and Food Safety Supervisor certification.

Interpersonal Skills: Outstanding leadership, communication, and conflict-resolution skills, with a strong ability to work under pressure during peak service times.

Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

About the Employer:
We are supporting a reliable cleaning services business (ABN 19 104 515 123) based in Darwin and surrounding areas, operating across commercial, residential, hospitality, aged care, and Airbnb cleaning. The business is known for quality service, attention to detail, safety, and customer satisfaction. With a growing team and service locations across multiple sites, they are seeking an Office Manager to oversee daily office operations, administration, customer enquiries, staff scheduling, records management, office systems, and general business support.

Key Responsibilities
- Organise and control daily office operations, administrative systems, and workflows to ensure efficient service delivery.
- Allocate and manage office resources, including staff, workspace, equipment, and supplies.
- Supervise, support, and monitor the performance of administrative and clerical staff.

- Support personnel activities including recruitment coordination, onboarding, training, leave records, and performance management processes

Selection Criteria
- Office administration expertise: Demonstrated experience managing office operations, systems, and administrative staff.
- People management: Proven ability to supervise, allocate tasks, and monitor staff performance.
- Organisational skills: Strong time management, prioritisation, and attention to detail across multiple tasks.
- Communication: Clear, professional communication with internal teams, management, and external stakeholders.
- Compliance & WHS awareness: Understanding of workplace policies, WHS obligations, and administrative compliance requirements.
- Problem-solving: Ability to identify operational issues and implement practical solutions.

Required Experience and Qualifications
- At least 2–3 years’ relevant experience in an office administration or office management role.
- Qualifications at AQF Diploma level or higher in Business Administration, Management, or a related field (preferred).

How to Apply
We are looking for a reliable, organised, and proactive Office Manager to join us and oversee the smooth day-to-day administration and office operations of our cleaning services business.

- A short cover letter of no more than 300 words explaining:
- Why you are applying for this position; and
- An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork. Please use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
- A written response of no more than 600 words describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the Office Manager role. Please structure your example or examples using the STAR method.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a reliable and growing cleaning services business that values quality, care, safety, and customer satisfaction, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Phone calls and walk-in applications will not be accepted.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 







We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 







As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 







Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network.



Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.





To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.


Help shape the future of healthcare at Monash Health and embark on a rewarding career where your dedication makes a difference in people's lives.



About the Role



Join our team as an Environmental Services Assistant on a part time ongoing to work at The Victorian Heart Hospital, based in Clayton. In this role, you will be guided under the leadership of the General Services Manager, and working with the broader Support Services team.



ESAs are responsible for maintaining a clean, hygienic, and safe hospital environment; not only for patients, but also for visitors and colleagues across Monash Health. ESAs deliver high-quality environmental services across clinical and non-clinical areas.



Key responsibilities include, but not limited to:




Ensuring adherence to infection prevention and control protocols at all times


Adhering to safety protocols when using cleaning chemicals and equipment in line with safety guidelines


Managing waste removal and disposal procedures safely and responsibly


Maintaining cleaning schedules and documentation


Reporting maintenance or safety hazards promptly


Collaborating with clinical and support teams to deliver service excellence


Completing relevant workplace training modules 


Distribution and collection of linen


Physical work including lifting and manual handling




We currently have the following opportunities available:



Position 1:


Days: Saturday-Tuesday


Hours: 6.30-15.00 (8hrs)


Total hours per fortnight: 64

Hours: 1430-2300 (8hrs)


Total hours per fortnight: 32

Total hours per fortnight: 16



 Position 5 


 Days: Saturday & Sunday 


 Hours :06:30- 15:00 (8hrs)


 Total hours Per fortnight: 32 



About You



To ensure your success in this role, you will bring experience in environmental services within a hospital, Aged Care or commercial cleaning setting with strong demonstrated knowledge of infection control and hygiene practices. You are a reliable and punctual team member with great verbal and written communication skills. Whether you're work independently or as part of a team; you always follow manual handling, safety protocols, and procedural instructions.



Why you will love working with us



As an ESA, you will play a vital role in supporting patient care while working within a supportive and inclusive team culture. Monash Health offers ongoing opportunities for professional development and leadership training. ESAs benefit from job stability within Victoria's largest public health service, along with clear career pathways across environmental and support services.



As a Monash Health employee you will enjoy a variety of benefits, such as:




Salary packaging options to increase your take-home pay


Novated leasing for vehicle options


Full-time employees accrue 5 week's annual leave (pro rata for part-time employees) 


Free annual flu vaccinations


Uniform and laundry allowance




About the Department - Program



The Support Services team is a collaborative and dedicated group that plays a crucial role in maintaining a safe, clean, and welcoming environment for patients, visitors, and staff. Our culture is built on respect, compassion, and excellence, and we are committed to continuous improvement and professional development.


 About Victorian Heart Hospital:


Australia's first dedicated cardiac hospital, located in Clayton at Monash University's Clayton campus. It offers world-class cardiovascular care, research, and education, with advanced facilities for cardiac procedures, imaging, and specialist treatment.




For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Amanda Deprinse 0488 387 021. 



Position Description can be found here




Our Culture and Values 







At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 







Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 







You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 







We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 







We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. 





How to Apply



Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system. For information including how to apply and probity check requirements, please click here for the 'Application Guide'



Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date.

The Team

The Central Intake and Referral Service, including the Medicare Mental Health (formerly Head to Health) phone service, was developed as a single, statewide intake and assessment phone service that integrates with Tasmania's existing state-based systems.

Working in a multidisciplinary environment, the Central Intake and Referral Service collaborates with healthcare providers and community partners to deliver timely, coordinated, and person-centred support, improving access and outcomes for the Tasmanian community.
